hypothesis: If a favourable mutation's sweep removes variation at linked neutral sites, and more so where recombination is weaker relative to selection, then across windows of a human chromosome nucleotide diversity should be positively correlated with the local recombination rate.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Data: 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3 chromosome 22 genotype VCF (release 20130502, all 2504 samples) and the HapMap Phase II GRCh37 genetic map for chromosome 22. SNP filter: records with VT=SNP in INFO, biallelic (no MULTI_ALLELIC flag, single ALT), FILTER PASS. Windows: non-overlapping 200 kb windows starting at 16,000,000 bp (GRCh37) up to the last SNP. Diversity per window: pi = sum over SNPs of 2p(1-p) * 2n/(2n-1), with p the INFO AF value and 2n = 5008 chromosomes, divided by the window length (200,000 bp). Windows with fewer than 200 qualifying SNPs are excluded as unassessable (centromere-proximal or low-accessibility regions). Recombination rate per window: (map cM at window end minus map cM at window start) / 0.2 Mb, with cM linearly interpolated from the genetic map. SUPPORTS if Spearman rho(pi, recombination rate) across windows is >= 0.2 with two-sided p < 0.01.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if rho < 0 with p < 0.05 (diversity lower where recombination is higher) OR if |rho| < 0.1 with p > 0.05 and at least 100 windows (no detectable relationship). MIXED otherwise (0 <= rho < 0.2, or 0.01 <= p). INCONCLUSIVE (data-unavailable) if either file cannot be downloaded.
interpretation: Maynard Smith and Haigh predicted that a sweep reduces heterozygosity at a linked neutral site by an amount that grows as recombination fraction over selection coefficient falls. The claim's assessment proposes the genome-wide version of the test used by Begun and Aquadro (1992): correlation between neutral diversity and local recombination rate. A positive correlation is also produced by background selection (Charlesworth et al. 1993), so a positive result supports the pattern the claim predicts but does not identify hitchhiking as the only cause; this is recorded as a caveat, not folded into the verdict. pi is computed from allele frequencies pooled across 26 populations; population structure inflates pooled pi roughly uniformly along the chromosome and does not create a correlation with recombination. All SNPs are used rather than only 'neutral' sites, which if anything weakens the expected correlation.

datasets.name: 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3 integrated variant call set, chromosome 22 (release 20130502, 2504 samples, GRCh37)
datasets.license: open (Fort Lauderdale principles; IGSR terms of use)
datasets.role: allele frequencies (INFO AF) of biallelic PASS SNPs for per-window nucleotide diversity

datasets.name: HapMap Phase II LD-based recombination map lifted to GRCh37 (NCBI HapMap FTP, 2011-01 release)
datasets.role: cumulative genetic position (cM) to compute recombination rate per 200 kb window

method: fetch.py downloads the chr22 VCF (205.6 MB) and the genetic-map archive. analysis.py streams the VCF, keeps PASS biallelic records with VT=SNP and without MULTI_ALLELIC, sums 2p(1-p)*2n/(2n-1) from the INFO AF value over non-overlapping 200 kb windows from 16.0 Mb, divides by window length to get pi, and takes the recombination rate per window from the linearly interpolated HapMap map; windows with fewer than 200 SNPs are excluded. Spearman and Pearson correlations between pi and rate across windows are computed and the pre-registered rule applied.

measured.unit: Spearman rho between per-window nucleotide diversity and recombination rate (cM/Mb), chr22, 200 kb windows

caveats: A positive diversity-recombination correlation is also produced by background selection (purifying selection removing linked neutral variation), so the result supports the pattern hitchhiking predicts but does not isolate sweeps as the cause; separating the two needs site-frequency or sweep-scan evidence.

Diversity is computed from allele frequencies pooled over all 26 populations; population structure inflates pi uniformly and does not create the correlation, but the absolute pi values are not a single-population estimate.

All SNPs are used, not only neutral sites; gene density and GC content covary with recombination in humans and could contribute to the correlation through mutation-rate variation. Windows with < 200 SNPs (none on chr22 above 16 Mb) would have been excluded.
One chromosome (22, about 35 Mb of assessable sequence) was tested, as pre-registered, to keep the download small; the pattern is well known genome-wide (Hellmann et al. 2003).
